Subject: Quantify AI onboarding — model slate & sizing

Hi Anya —

Thanks again for the kickoff earlier. To keep momentum, I'm sending a concise proposal for the initial model shortlist and a first-pass token-volume worksheet (attached) so engineering can begin sizing. High level: Quantify wants real‑time summarization in the app and a nightly batch analytics pipeline — those have different latency and cost profiles, so we recommend 2 model tiers.

Quick asks for us to finalize sizing:
- Confirm expected concurrent interactive sessions during peak (e.g., 200, 1k).
- Typical user prompt + expected average response length (tokens).
- Any PII-sensitive fields that must be redacted before hitting hosted inference.

Attached: initial_token_profile.xlsx — contains current event assumptions we pulled from the kickoff. I’ve proposed three candidate models (details below) and a recommended default for Hosted vs Dedicated lanes.

Candidate models (initial):
- Redwood-Delta-7B-int8 — low cost, good latency for short responses (recommended for interactive fallback).
- Redwood-Orbit-13B-q5 — middle ground; strong instruction following for summarization.
- Open-Scale-70B-fp16 — higher quality for batch-heavy, long-context analytics (consider dedicated capacity).

Suggested next steps:
1) You confirm the numbers above (concurrency, avg tokens).
2) We run a short benchmark (3 days) on two user flows: interactive summaries and nightly analytic aggregation.
3) We lock initial rollout model + caching window.

I’ll wait on the concurrency/avg token answers and will book a 30m sizing call if that’s easiest.

Cheers,

Thanks Mina — this is great and aligns with what we discussed. Quick answers:
- Peak concurrency: we expect ~450 concurrent interactive users during peak business hours (Eastern).
- Typical prompt/response: prompts average ~60 tokens; responses average ~220 tokens for summaries.
- Nightly analytic jobs: ~3M tokens/day aggregated across pipelines (we can provide logs if you need distribution).
- PII: we have user-submitted documents that may contain names and phone numbers; for now we prefer token redaction on the client before sending to the API. Full on‑hosted PII handling will be a later phase.

A couple clarifying Qs:
1) For the interactive lane, is Redwood-Delta-7B-int8 expected to meet the 220-token output SLA at p95 latency < 350ms?
2) For the batch analytics, do you recommend quantized variants of the 70B model or running fp16 on Dedicated?

If helpful, Raj and I are available for a 30m call tomorrow morning (9–11am PT).

Anya —

Good context, thanks. Short answers to your Qs and a couple of operational notes:

1) Latency: Redwood-Delta-7B-int8 should meet ~p50 60–80ms and p95 depends on batching and prefix cache hit-rate. For a 220-token output at p95 < 350ms we recommend:
   - Keep batching small for interactive lane (max batch size 8–16).
   - Enable prefix/KV cache with 5m TTL for repeated prompts.
   - Route from the US-east region to avoid cross-region penalty.

2) Batch analytics: quantized 70B (q4/q5) often gives strong cost-performance tradeoffs for throughput; however, if you need absolute best quality for long-context aggregation (>=8k tokens), fp16 on Dedicated with optimized kernels is safer. Quick rule: quantized for cost-sensitive nightly jobs; fp16 for accuracy/consistency-sensitive models.

Operational checklist I’ll run with Grace/Kimberly once you confirm concurrency:
- Benchmark matrix (models x token lengths x routing lanes)
- Cache window experiment plan
- Estimate of monthly token spend and projected Dedicated sizing if >10M tokens/month at sustained throughput

I’ve attached a small ops note that Grace prepared.

Mina

Looping in some ops detail. We expect the first benchmark run to take ~48 hours and we'll capture:
- p50/p95 token latency per model variant (interactive workloads)
- throughput and GPU utilization for batch jobs (tokens/sec)
- cache hit rates and effective token savings

Notes / recommendations:
- For interactive lane, start with max_batch=12, queue_timeout=30ms; tune down if p95 spikes.
- For nightly jobs, set concurrency per-worker to 4 and use micro-batching to saturate GPU kernels.
- Instrumentation: we’ll add a temporary tracing hook to the route and provide a per-token cost dashboard for the pilot window.
